_note: STARTING POINT — curated by ClauseWise maintainers. Review and extend before each release. Not legal advice; used only for severity comparison within the tool.

typical_patterns.typical: Clearly defined category of information (e.g., marked 'Confidential', or specific types listed). Oral disclosures confirmed in writing within 30 days.
red_flags: all information exchanged between parties is confidential regardless of marking
no definition provided
includes publicly available information
receiving party must prove information was public even if obviously so

typical_patterns.typical: 2–5 years from disclosure for commercial NDAs. Perpetual only for trade secrets.
red_flags: perpetual obligation on all information regardless of type
duration extends indefinitely unless disclosing party releases
no expiry for general business information not qualifying as trade secrets

typical_patterns.typical: Excludes: (1) information already public, (2) info already known by receiving party, (3) info received from a third party lawfully, (4) independently developed without reference to confidential info.
red_flags: no carve-outs at all
receiving party bears burden of proof for all carve-outs with onerous requirements
carve-outs require prior written consent of disclosing party

typical_patterns.typical: Disclosure to employees/advisors on need-to-know basis, bound by equivalent confidentiality. Disclosure required by law allowed with notice to disclosing party where legally possible.
red_flags: no provision for legal compulsion to disclose
disclosure to any third party prohibited regardless of court order
receiving party must indemnify for any compelled disclosure

typical_patterns.typical: Injunctive relief and actual damages available. Parties acknowledge breach causes irreparable harm (boilerplate, standard). No punitive multipliers.
red_flags: fixed penalty per breach regardless of actual harm
liquidated damages clause with a very high amount
receiving party responsible for all breaches by its employees regardless of fault or instruction

typical_patterns.typical: Confidential information used only for the stated purpose (e.g., evaluating a partnership, conducting due diligence).
red_flags: no stated purpose; information may be used for any purpose by receiving party
permitted use expands without notice
receiving party can use information to compete

typical_patterns.typical: On request or termination, receiving party returns or certifiably destroys confidential materials. Backup copies excluded from instant deletion with reasonable retention cap.
red_flags: no return/destruction obligation
receiving party may retain copies indefinitely
destruction at disclosing party's expense
